sections.heading: 1. Build a parcel-first public-record spine
paragraphs: Begin with a dated county tax-roll export and a separate surplus ledger, preserving each source's retrieval date, assessment year, field definitions, and update cadence. Normalize assessor parcel numbers without losing leading zeros, suffixes, or the county identifier; an APN is not globally unique. Keep situs address separate from owner mailing address, and preserve original owner text before creating normalized matching fields. Join sale cases to parcels using both identifiers and legal descriptions, flagging splits, combinations, and condominium units for review. A tax-roll owner can lag a recorded transfer, so a successful join is a research lead rather than proof of entitlement. Maintain one internal case identifier linking the raw row, sale record, recorder evidence, and later claimant research.

County Recorder Grantor/Grantee indexes answer who recorded which instrument and when. Search the former owner's exact name, common variants, trust capacities, and entity names in both directions, then obtain the deed, mortgage, assignment, release, or notice image associated with each relevant index entry. Document book and page or instrument number so another researcher can reproduce the finding. The Tax Assessor APN roll contributes land use, assessed values, tax districts, exemptions, building attributes, and mailing data, but those fields do not establish clean title or current contactability. When the recorder and assessor disagree, retain both versions and explain the effective dates. Do not silently overwrite a deed-derived owner with a more recent commercial enrichment result that merely repeats the assessor feed.

Regrid can accelerate parcel geometry, address matching, and geographic review; DataTree can help locate property records, vesting information, and document products where its coverage supports the county. Treat both as discovery and retrieval layers whose specific fields, permissions, and update dates must be checked. A boundary drawn on a map is not a survey, and a cached owner name is not a certified vesting finding. Use a source register to distinguish original county evidence from vendor transformations and manually corrected values. For bulk work, use available official exports, documented APIs, or licensed downloads within their terms, and retain the original record identifier beside the normalized one. This makes a parcel mismatch repairable without rebuilding the entire investigative file from memory.

sections.heading: 2. Search bankruptcy and entity authority before outreach
paragraphs: Run a bankruptcy search before contacting a former owner about an available fund. Use the PACER Case Locator and appropriate bankruptcy court docket, searching name variants and corroborating matches with lawful identifiers such as addresses, filing jurisdiction, or entity details. A common name match is not enough to label someone a debtor. Capture the petition date, chapter, case status, trustee, debtor counsel, and docket entries relevant to the property or proceeds. For an open Chapter 7 case, identify the trustee and examine schedules, exemption claims, sale orders, abandonment notices, and any order addressing surplus. For Chapter 13, identify the trustee and read the plan and confirmation order, because property-of-estate and vesting treatment can depend on the plan, statute, and controlling decisions.

Section 541 of title 11 broadly defines bankruptcy estate property, including many interests held at commencement and certain proceeds, but it does not tell a researcher that every post-sale dollar automatically belongs to the debtor or trustee. Analyze when the ownership interest and surplus right arose, whether exemptions apply, and whether property was properly abandoned or otherwise dealt with by order. A discharge is not proof that an unadministered asset has returned to the debtor; an unscheduled asset can remain estate property after closing. Record uncertainty and direct authority questions to the appropriate representative or counsel before solicitation or an agreement concerning the asset. Separate locating a person from advising them to transfer or collect property that may be controlled by the bankruptcy estate.

For entity-owned parcels, search Secretary of State filings in the formation jurisdiction and any relevant foreign registration jurisdiction. Officer, manager, registered-agent, annual-report, merger, and dissolution records help identify a current point of contact, but a registered agent's service address is not necessarily an operational office or authority to sign a recovery agreement. Cross-check the entity number, exact name, historical names, and filing dates against the deed and bankruptcy results. Where public filings omit members or use outdated officials, request current authority documents rather than guessing. Save a short authority memorandum naming the apparent claimant, evidence supporting that conclusion, unresolved questions, and the next document required. This prevents the skip-tracing team from pursuing a former employee while the actual entity is in receivership or bankruptcy.

sections.heading: 3. Operate a corroborated skip-tracing waterfall
paragraphs: Start the waterfall with low-cost public evidence: deed mailing addresses, assessor correspondence addresses, filed court contacts, entity filings, and public obituary information. An obituary may connect a deceased owner to relatives or reveal a changed surname, but it does not establish heirship or authorize contacting every person listed. Compare address histories by date and distinguish residence, business, mailing service, and care-facility addresses. Use forwarding information only through authorized postal services or lawfully obtained records; a return-mail annotation is a lead, not a license to obtain restricted postal data. Document the source and date of each candidate address, and keep a deceased indicator separate from a confirmed death record. This preserves useful leads without letting an inference overwrite verified identity evidence.

Next use a licensed people-search or skip-tracing product under a documented permissible purpose, then corroborate the result against at least one genuinely independent source. Wireless numbers, landlines, household members, and relatives should each carry a source, observed date, and confidence reason. Two vendors selling the same underlying telephone feed are one evidentiary lineage, not two independent confirmations. A shared surname and nearby address are weak support for a recycled mobile number; a consistent historical address chain plus a separate current public filing is stronger. Rank contacts by recency and agreement, set aside contradictory records, and record wrong-party responses promptly. For relatives, use a limited locating inquiry without disclosing the surplus amount or sensitive financial circumstances, and do not imply that the relative has any claim to the money.

Before outreach, review the intended contact channel against applicable calling, texting, do-not-call, and professional solicitation rules. A vendor's verified label does not supply consent or establish that an automated dialing campaign is permitted. Use a neutral first message identifying the business and inviting the intended recipient to verify the matter through the official custodian. Do not publish sensitive identifiers or attach probate and bankruptcy documents to an unverified contact. Confirm identity through proportionate evidence before discussing the claim in detail, then move documents into a restricted case file. Track returned mail, wrong numbers, refusals, and contact preferences in a suppression record shared across the team. This turns the waterfall into a controlled investigation rather than repeated outreach to every purchased contact associated with a surname.

sections.heading: 4. Respect data boundaries and reuse the roll for assessment appeals
paragraphs: The Driver's Privacy Protection Act, 18 U.S.C. section 2721, limits disclosure and use of personal information from motor vehicle records to specified exceptions. Ordinary surplus prospecting is not automatically one of them, and a business identity does not create blanket access. Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act restrictions and its prohibition on obtaining financial customer information through false pretenses likewise do not disappear because a vendor sells a search box. Require the actual source, applicable purpose, and contractual permission for restricted datasets; omit them where the purpose is unsupported. The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, 18 U.S.C. section 1030, addresses unauthorized computer access and related conduct. Use authorized credentials and permitted interfaces without bypassing access controls. Public availability, contractual permission, and statutory permitted use are distinct questions that deserve separate records.

Reuse the same versioned county tax-roll pipeline for Track 01 Operator Play property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency, Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage. This is an adjacent service for authorized owners, not a reason to represent former owners after they have lost the property. Screen assessed values against independently supported market values or uniformity measures allowed locally, using the correct valuation date and assessment ratio. Segment residential properties by neighborhood, size, age, condition, and sale validity; segment commercial properties by use, occupancy, income evidence, and capitalization assumptions where relevant. Automation can rank anomalies and assemble comparable candidates, but someone must inspect comparability, exemptions, equalization factors, and filing deadlines. Maintain separate engagements and permissions for appeals and surplus recovery even when both originate from one parcel record.

The Valuation-Rejection Trap is filing an appeal supported by attractive but irrelevant sales, such as renovated houses outside the assessment neighborhood or commercial transfers with unusual financing. The Comparable-Equity Ratio Fallback is a documented uniformity argument only where that appeal basis is recognized: use similar properties, explain exclusions, calculate consistent assessment-to-market ratios, and reconcile material differences. Suppose the subject's supported market value is $1,000,000, its assessment is $300,000, and a valid comparable analysis supports a 22.5% assessment ratio. The modeled target is $225,000, a $75,000 reduction. At an effective 2.4% tax rate on the assessment reduction, annual savings would be $1,800; a permitted 25% realized-savings fee would be $450. Check caps, exemptions, tax-rate mechanics, and actual bills before invoicing, and revalidate annually rather than assuming an automatic recurring award.

chapters.title: Ethical Outreach, Statutory Fee Caps & Attorney-Escrow Contracting
chapters.subtitle: Navigating state fee ceilings, post-sale waiting periods, mobile notary packets, and anti-fraud disclosures.
chapters.executive_summary: A surplus lead is a public record, not permission to promise payment or purchase an owner's rights. Build the engagement around the sale type, the controlling statute, the documented claimant, and a transparent distribution statement. This chapter separates judicial foreclosure from tax-deed claims, compares five state pathways, and turns outreach into a reproducible evidence trail. It also explains why an attorney trust account cannot rescue an unlawful fee or forged assignment. The operating objective is a valid claim with informed owner participation, defensible deductions, and independently confirmed disbursement instructions.

sections.heading: Classify the sale before pricing the engagement
paragraphs: Start with the instrument that created the fund, not the county's marketing label. Obtain the tax deed or certificate of title, final judgment when applicable, sale confirmation, surplus deposit entry, and the clerk's current claim instructions. Record the sale date separately from the deposit date and the date any notice was mailed. A judicial foreclosure surplus and a tax-deed surplus in the same Florida county do not share one interchangeable procedure. Identify which event starts each statutory clock and preserve the underlying document beside the calculated deadline. A spreadsheet populated from an auction date alone can produce a perfectly formatted contract that addresses the wrong fund and the wrong claimant.

Florida section 45.033 concerns judicial foreclosure surplus ownership, assignments, and surplus-trustee requirements; section 197.582 addresses tax-deed surplus distribution and claims. Texas section 34.04 requires special attention to both capped recovery compensation and post-sale assignment restrictions. California Civil Code sections 2924j and 2924k govern trustee-sale distribution, while Revenue and Taxation Code section 4675 supplies a different tax-sale claim and assignment framework. Georgia section 48-4-5 addresses tax-sale excess funds and competing interests. Ohio and Pennsylvania require the actual court docket, controlling distribution rules, and local motion practice. Never infer that a state lacking a percentage in this comparison permits any desired fee or allows an unlicensed operator to represent claimants in court.

Treat the comparison as a routing document rather than a reusable contract opinion. Counsel must identify the current statutory text, subsection, effective date, county procedure, applicable deadline, and whether the proposed arrangement is a service agreement, assignment, or legal representation. Keep those classifications separate in the engagement record. The assignment buyer's purchase price is not automatically a permissible recovery-service charge, and renaming compensation does not change its substance. For Texas, a covered $98,000 recovery would not support an ordinary $24,500 collection fee under the lesser-of cap: the arithmetic ceiling is $1,000. Model economics only after the legal service structure is settled, and decline files whose lawful proceeds cannot support delivery costs.

sections.heading: Make the first contact transparent and traceable
paragraphs: Use an opening that distinguishes the public deposit from the owner's eventual entitlement: 'We are a private recovery service, not the county or a court. The county record dated June 4 lists $142,000 in gross surplus connected to this sale. Liens and other claims may reduce or exhaust that amount. You can ask the clerk about claiming directly without hiring us. We charge no upfront fee under our proposed contingent arrangement, and we will provide the fee and expense terms in writing before you decide.' Include the official office name and a public contact route the owner can independently locate. Never describe the entire deposit as an approved payment already belonging to the recipient.

Before telephone outreach, classify the channel, number source, dialing method, message content, and applicable federal and state requirements. A public property record does not establish consent for automated marketing calls, prerecorded voices, or texts. Scrub against relevant national and state do-not-call lists, maintain an internal suppression list, observe calling-hour limits, and retain the scrub date with the campaign version. Honor revocation and stop requests across vendors rather than merely deleting one phone field. Manual calls are not a blanket exemption from solicitation restrictions. Where the contact basis is uncertain, use a plainly branded letter with the clerk's direct-claim route rather than testing whether a disputed call produces a complaint.

Record the precise script, contact date, recipient identity confidence, and outcome without collecting unnecessary sensitive identifiers. If a relative answers, request a safe contact route instead of announcing a deceased owner's assets or alleged entitlement. For returned mail, investigate the address using authorized sources and preserve the uncertainty instead of escalating to repeated calls. Offer a written comparison of self-filing, independent counsel, and the proposed recovery service. Explain whether any expense is deducted before or after the contingent percentage and whether the owner owes anything if nothing is recovered. Give the recipient time to verify the county record independently; urgency should describe an actual documented filing deadline, never an invented expiration on an offer.

sections.heading: Build a verifiable packet and a lawful trust-account waterfall
paragraphs: The packet should identify the actual service provider, the claimant, the specific sale and fund, the agreed scope, and every compensation recipient. Include the written contingency terms, expense treatment, direct-claim explanation, narrowly scoped authorizations, and any assignment disclosures required for that transaction. Counsel must distinguish assistance gathering records from legal advice and court representation. Do not assume that adding an attorney signature cures unauthorized legal work or permits sharing legal fees with a nonlawyer. A research vendor can have a separately lawful compensation arrangement, but the invoice, engagement, and distribution statement must describe what actually happened. Do not split one prohibited recovery fee into several smaller invoices to conceal the combined charge from the owner or court.

A mobile notary verifies the appearance and identity required under the governing notarization law; the notary does not establish title, inheritance, claim priority, or contract fairness. Send a versioned packet with no blank economic terms, verify the venue and permitted identification method, and match the signer's name against the claim documents. For an estate, trust, or company, obtain the relevant letters, trust authority, resolution, or other authority evidence in addition to personal identification. Retain the completed certificate and legally appropriate audit record without copying unnecessary identity documents. If the owner denies a signature, stop using that instrument, preserve the original scan and transmission history, and have counsel determine the correction and notification path rather than asking a notary to backdate a replacement.

When permitted, counsel receives recovered funds in the appropriate attorney trust account; IOLTA is appropriate only where the jurisdiction's rules and expected holding circumstances call for it. Larger or longer-held client funds may require a separate interest-bearing account. Confirm the account holder and disbursement instructions through an independently verified office number, not an emailed replacement instruction. Maintain an individual client ledger showing cleared receipts, lien payments, authorized fees, reimbursable expenses, and the owner's distribution. Counsel should retain disputed amounts as required while releasing undisputed funds when permitted. The owner receives a settlement statement reconciling the original deposit to every deduction. The recovery company never treats the entire client receipt as its own revenue or advances money against uncleared trust funds.

sections.heading: Forensic teardown: three traps and an evidence-backed fallback
paragraphs: The illegal upfront-fee trap often begins with an official-looking notice promising release of a specific check after an owner pays a processing charge. Examine the envelope, payment recipient, asserted agency relationship, and cited authority. Compare the supposed fee with the clerk's published schedule and the actual engagement. Do not imply every advance professional retainer is unlawful everywhere; the defect may instead be a prohibited recovery charge, deception, or charging for a nonexistent release. In this operating model the owner pays zero upfront, the firm funds agreed investigation, and counsel confirms what compensation is lawful on success. Preserve questionable notices as evidence, remove their claims from the sales script, and route any refund or reporting decision through verified counsel rather than forwarding more money to the sender.

The forged-assignment trap attacks ownership rather than merely price. Warning signs include an execution date inconsistent with a statutory waiting period, a signature denied by the named owner, an unexplained address change, a mismatched notarial venue, or an agent unable to produce authority. Compare the assignment against the recorded ownership chain and original transmission metadata; do not certify authenticity from visual similarity alone. A fresh notarization cannot retroactively make a forged transfer genuine. The deceptive-government-mailer trap instead borrows seals, court formatting, threatening deadlines, or words such as mandatory to manufacture authority. Replace it with the firm's actual name, an accurate private-service description, documented deadlines, and the independently verifiable public claim route. Preserve the misleading original without reusing it as a conversion template.

The fallback is a verified claimant, a documented fund, independently retained counsel where required, and a transparent escrow distribution, not a cleverer assignment form. If an owner disputes a contract, pause use of that contract and let counsel establish whether a new lawful engagement or direct claim is appropriate. If a senior lien may consume the fund, update the recovery estimate before requesting a signature and avoid presenting a speculative fee as earned. Track a complaint against the exact campaign and packet versions so the same representation does not recur elsewhere. At closing, compare promised and actual deductions, record any variance explanation, and retain the final order and cleared-payment evidence. A trustworthy process is demonstrated by a file that another examiner can reconstruct without relying on the salesperson's memory.

chapters.subtitle: Turn fragmented county PDF overage lists into underwritten claim dossiers with human title sign-off.
chapters.executive_summary: Automate collection and reconciliation, not the conclusion that a named person owns a surplus. A dependable pipeline preserves county source files, reconstructs tables with page and row provenance, enriches parcel and entity identifiers, and sends uncertain evidence to a human title examiner. The worked case follows a $142,000 deposit through priority deductions, a conditional 25% fee, direct costs, and a contested loss. Its economics are illustrative rather than a universal contract template. The practical advantage is a smaller team producing reviewable dossiers while preventing duplicate contacts, invented lien conclusions, and premature revenue recognition.

sections.heading: Watch authorized sources without turning collection into intrusion
paragraphs: Create one source registry entry for each permitted county auction calendar, excess-proceeds PDF directory, and downloadable CSV. Store the office name, public URL, permission or published usage conditions, expected update cadence, and contact for obtaining bulk records. Prefer official downloads, documented interfaces, or requested exports over fragile page traversal. A weekly list does not need minute-by-minute polling. Use conditional requests where supported, conservative timeouts, response-size limits, bounded retries, and backoff after throttling. If authentication, a CAPTCHA, or an access restriction appears, stop that collection route and seek an authorized export instead of rotating identities or bypassing the restriction. Record the gap so silence is not mistaken for zero new surplus.

Each successful fetch becomes an immutable source snapshot with retrieval time, source publication date if available, response metadata, byte length, and a SHA-256 digest of the original bytes. Compare digests before parsing so an unchanged report does not create fresh leads. Never replace yesterday's report silently: counties correct amounts, withdraw entries, and move funds between reporting periods. Link a new version to the previous snapshot and compute field-level differences. A removed row means absent from this version, not necessarily paid. A calendar entry means scheduled, not sold; require a completed-sale record and actual deposit evidence before a prospect advances toward a claim dossier.

The collection policy should address authorization independently of whether a page is publicly reachable. Section 1030 concerns unauthorized access and exceeding authorized access; its application depends on facts, and it is not a blanket prohibition on all scraping. Terms, privacy duties, and other laws may impose separate constraints. Keep authorization evidence and operational limits alongside the source configuration. Do not upload owner identifiers or complete dossiers to an external AI service merely because the source document was public. For optional document assistance, use a specifically authorized processing environment, minimize fields, and retain the model output as a suggestion linked to evidence rather than as a new public record.

sections.heading: Extract tables deterministically and enrich identifiers cautiously
paragraphs: Parse a real CSV with a standards-aware reader and preserve quoted commas, empty cells, encoding information, and the original header map. For PDFs, extract embedded text first; send only image-only or unusable pages through an approved OCR process. The chapter describes that process, not a claim that Python's standard library provides an OCR engine. Anchor regular expressions to known county formats for parcel identifiers, dates, currency, and case numbers. Do not use a general currency match as the final surplus field when one row also includes bid price, taxes, and costs. Maintain separate fields for raw text, normalized value, confidence reason, and any human correction.

Compute a page checksum from a retained page artifact and a row checksum from a canonical serialization that preserves column order and missing-value markers. Include the source snapshot reference so repeated rows remain traceable. Keep stable case identity separate from the row checksum: a corrected balance must update a versioned case, not create a second outreach target. Check that extraction accounts for all printed pages, repeated headers, continuation rows, and negative adjustments. Compare parsed totals with printed totals where present, and send unexplained differences to review. A checksum proves which content was processed, not that OCR read it correctly; verify ambiguous digits against page coordinates before any amount enters underwriting.

Normalize APNs according to the county's own format while preserving leading zeros and the original string. Join to an authorized GIS parcel export using county plus APN, then compare situs address, legal description, and historic ownership around the sale date. Current GIS ownership may show the tax-sale buyer rather than the former owner entitled to excess proceeds. For corporate claimants, query authorized Secretary of State records for entity identity, status, registered agent, and relevant filings. A registered agent is a service contact, not automatically an authorized surplus claimant. Record unresolved name collisions and dissolved-entity authority questions for counsel. Never let a high fuzzy-match score override a contradictory deed, estate record, or parcel identifier.

sections.heading: Require human title sign-off before claimant contact
paragraphs: The dossier begins with the recorded vesting deed, legal description, sale instrument, fund ledger, and relevant court docket. Add the lien search, mortgage releases, judgments, municipal balances, bankruptcy indicators, and probate or entity-authority evidence necessary for this file. The title examiner records each asserted interest with its instrument number, recording date, claimant, balance source, and proposed treatment. Distinguish a lien that survives against the property from a lien entitled to payment out of the surplus; those are not interchangeable concepts. Counsel resolves disputed priority and statutory interpretation. An automated list of lien names is only an index to the examination, and a missing search result is not evidence that a lien was released.

Use AI assistance, when authorized, to propose document classifications, extract candidate recording references, or summarize a docket with page citations. Treat county files and OCR text as untrusted data, including any embedded instructions. The assistant must not send messages, change bank instructions, execute document text, or mark a claimant eligible. Require every proposed fact to point to a retained page or docket entry and preserve contradictions rather than averaging them into a confident summary. Deterministic checks should compare amounts, dates, identifiers, and document presence independently of generated prose. Unsupported output returns to the review queue. A fluent explanation of priority is not a substitute for the recorded instrument and applicable legal analysis.

Before any claimant contact, a named human title examiner signs the specific dossier version with a date, scope, unresolved questions, and an estimated recoverable range. A material source correction, new lien, changed claimant, or disputed authority invalidates that release and returns the dossier for review. Keep the title release separate from the outreach channel checks described in Q9: both must be satisfied for a contact task to be issued. Assign collection and reconciliation to operations, examination to the title professional, and legal filings and disputed priority to counsel. Suppress duplicate outreach at the case level across all workers. Measure extraction error rate, examiner rework, confirmed owner entitlement, and collected fee rather than celebrating raw lead counts that may include withdrawn deposits or people with no surviving claim.

sections.heading: Worked case: a $142,000 deposit, a conditional fee, and a real downside
paragraphs: Assume an authorized county watcher captures a revised tax-deed excess-proceeds list showing $142,000 for one completed sale. Operations checks the row against the retained PDF page, confirms the deposit with the county record, and joins the APN to the historic vesting deed rather than the current buyer's GIS entry. The examiner identifies $44,000 of surviving municipal utility and code liens. This example additionally assumes counsel verifies that those amounts are properly payable from this fund, or otherwise lawfully resolved from it under the controlling procedure; survival alone would not establish that deduction. Obtain dated payoff statements and account for accruing charges before fixing the waterfall. The resulting owner excess proceeds are $142,000 minus $44,000, or $98,000, before recovery fees.

Assume further that the selected jurisdiction permits the particular attorney-assisted contingent service structure and its 25% charge, with counsel confirming the aggregate fee treatment and professional-conduct constraints. This is not a Texas section 34.04 covered recovery-service example: its lesser-of-25%-or-$1,000 ceiling would defeat the proposed $24,500 fee. Do not evade that limit by describing a collection agreement as an assignment. After title sign-off and permitted outreach, the owner receives the gross fund amount, documented deductions, direct-claim option, written scope, and compensation terms. Identity and authority are verified in the completed mobile notary packet. Counsel files the appropriate claim, resolves the priority treatment, and obtains the distribution authority before recognizing a successful recovery.

The modeled fee is 25% of $98,000, producing $24,500 gross fee and $73,500 for the owner after that fee. The business bears $3,500 for partner surplus counsel, $650 for the full title abstract, $250 for mobile notary and overnight courier, $1,250 for research and operations labor, and $1,200 allocated from the dead-lead cohort. Those costs total $6,850 and are not deducted a second time from the owner's $73,500. The fee recipient and each professional's payment must follow the lawful engagement structure; this economic budget does not authorize splitting legal fees with a nonlawyer. Cleared funds, the approved settlement statement, individual trust ledger, and payment evidence reconcile the full $142,000 before the file is closed.

Net contribution is $24,500 minus $6,850, or $17,650. Dividing by gross fee gives 72.0408%, displayed as 72.0%; dividing by the county deposit would answer a different question. This contribution excludes general overhead, taxes, and financing costs, so it is not owner net income. In the separate contested scenario, a verified senior-priority claim exhausts the available surplus before an owner distribution. The firm earns zero contingent fee and stops after $650 in abstract costs, $1,250 in research labor, and $500 in preliminary counsel review, producing a $2,400 loss. These are alternative failed-file costs, not another deduction from the successful file. Track them at cohort level without double-counting the successful model's dead-lead allocation, and update forecasts when actual loss frequency replaces the initial planning assumption.

chapters.title: Small-Team Scaling: Running a High-Margin 2-to-4 Person Recovery Firm
chapters.subtitle: Separating county list ingestion, title underwriting, claimant outreach, and outside motion counsel.
chapters.executive_summary: Scale surplus recovery by separating evidence collection, underwriting, claimant communication, and filing responsibility before adding counties. The Base model uses two full-time operators and two part-time contractors, with outside attorneys engaged per file rather than counted as permanent seats. Revenue follows collected fees, not listed balances or signed agreements. Weekly aging reconciliation exposes stalled disbursements; script audits protect communication accuracy; encrypted, restricted records reduce claimant-data exposure. Expand to three full-time operators and three contractors only when measured capacity, contribution margins, and a funded collection runway support the additional desk.

sections.heading: Four seats, explicit handoffs, and outside legal capacity
paragraphs: The four-person Base firm consists of a Principal/Underwriting Lead, a Full-Time Outreach & Claimant Specialist, a Part-Time County List & Title Abstractor, and a Part-Time Notary/Packet Coordinator. The first two positions are full-time; the latter two are modeled contractor seats, subject to actual worker classification. A network of per-file state surplus attorneys supplies outside motion counsel and is an expense, not a hidden fifth permanent employee. The principal decides whether the evidence supports spending more on a claim. The abstractor assembles records without deciding disputed legal priority. The specialist handles claimant communication, while the coordinator checks packet completeness and arranges execution. Nobody promises a payout merely because a county list contains a name.

Each file moves through named handoffs with an accountable sender and receiver. Ingestion delivers the official list date, county account identifier, sale type, stated balance, and source document. Abstracting delivers recorded vesting instruments, grantor and grantee searches, an ownership and encumbrance report, and a chronology of potentially surviving interests. Underwriting returns a written claimant hypothesis, estimated net distributable amount, unresolved priority questions, and a spending ceiling. Outreach receives only the contact data and approved factual explanation needed for that assignment. Packet coordination receives counsel's current document checklist. Counsel receives the evidence bundle and unresolved questions rather than an unsupported instruction to file immediately. A rejected handoff records the missing instrument and next responsible person.

Do not assume that calling the abstractor or coordinator a contractor settles employment status. Section 203 of Title 29 defines employee, employer, and employ broadly for federal wage-and-hour purposes; classification depends on the applicable legal framework and actual relationship, not a budget label. Review control, independence, scheduling, tools, and economic circumstances with appropriate advisers, including separate state requirements. Budget payroll treatment if the facts require it. A coordinator who is also a notary must follow the commissioning state's rules, avoid prohibited conflicts, and keep notarization distinct from explaining legal rights. Outside attorneys determine representation, filings, and legal strategy under their engagement terms. These boundaries preserve a lean operating model without substituting inexpensive administrative labor for licensed judgment.

sections.heading: Capacity economics before a six-person multi-state desk
paragraphs: The Base illustration collects $425,000 in annual gross fees and retains $148,750 at a 35 percent owner-net margin, leaving $276,250 for modeled operating costs. Gross fees are the firm's earned collections, not the claimant's surplus balance and not the face value of signed contracts. Specify whether principal compensation is included in costs before comparing actual results with this illustration; owner distributions cannot also appear as an additional operating expense. Record payroll, contractor invoices, counsel charges borne by the firm, title reports, tracing, software, insurance, and unrecovered acquisition spending consistently. An apparently excellent month can simply reflect old files paying together. Track originating cohorts beside cash receipts so that a collection spike does not masquerade as durable production.

The Multi-State illustration grows to three full-time staff and three contractor seats, collecting $750,000 in gross fees with $337,500 owner net at a 45 percent margin. Its cost ceiling is therefore $412,500 annually. Add a Full-Time Operations & Reconciliation Lead to the principal and outreach specialist, and add a second Part-Time County List & Title Abstractor to the existing abstractor and packet coordinator. The new operations lead owns queue control, aging, and quality sampling; the principal retains exception underwriting. Counsel remains an external per-file network with state-specific competence. The margin improvement is an assumption to test through throughput and purchased-service costs, not an automatic reward for entering another jurisdiction or hiring another operator.

Translate the revenue goal into observable capacity before increasing commitments. At an illustrative $8,500 average collected fee, the Base goal requires fifty paid files annually; at $10,000 per collected fee, the Multi-State goal requires seventy-five. Neither average is a proposed fee rate: lawful contract terms and actual claimant recoveries determine earned fees. If only half of counsel-ready files ultimately collect within the planning year, seventy-five collections require roughly one hundred fifty counsel-ready files, with opening backlog and timing modeled separately. Measure abstracting hours, outreach attempts, execution failures, and counsel turnaround on the current cohort. Purchase additional capacity at the measured bottleneck, not at the loudest complaint. Maintain a six-month operating reserve separately from expected but unpaid fees.

sections.heading: Weekly reconciliation turns aging claims into assigned work
paragraphs: Every Monday, reconcile the claim register against the clerk's docket, counsel's filing receipts, county disbursement communications, and the firm's bank receipts. Use calendar days since the clerk accepted a complete claim as the primary aging clock, while preserving sale date, contract date, statutory deadline, and last activity separately. Label buckets 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, and over 180 days so that every file belongs to exactly one bucket. Those are internal management intervals, not statutory payment promises. A pending objection may be normal in one county and urgent in another. Record the actual reason, next event, responsible party, and evidence date instead of changing the clock to make the report look younger.

For the first thirty days, confirm receipt, assigned claim number, and whether the clerk identified missing documents. At sixty days, seek a dated status update through counsel or the clerk's permitted channel and compare the case with its county's observed processing history. At ninety days, review unresolved service, competing claims, hearings, and proposed distribution calculations with counsel. At one hundred eighty days, reassess expected collection timing and reserve coverage without abandoning an otherwise viable claim. A deadline due tomorrow takes precedence over a young aging bucket. Separate funds ordered, funds issued, claimant funds received, and firm fees collected; these are different events. Never count the full county payment as firm revenue when most belongs to the claimant.

Make reconciliation a short exception meeting with documentary outputs. The operations owner identifies stale evidence, unexplained amount changes, duplicate county entries, and bank receipts that do not match the case ledger. The principal resolves spending changes; counsel owns legal responses; the specialist delivers claimant updates using verified facts. Reconcile opening receivables plus newly earned fees minus collections and supported adjustments to closing receivables, applying the firm's accounting policy consistently. Keep speculative pipeline outside that arithmetic. If a claimant receives funds directly, use authorized payment evidence and the contract to establish the fee due rather than treating silence as payment. A weekly signed reconciliation note should list exceptions, owners, due dates, and the specific records needed to close each item.

sections.heading: Audit communication and protect claimant records
paragraphs: Audit five outreach interactions per specialist each week, or every interaction when the week's volume is lower. Include at least one nonresponse sequence, one fee explanation, and one disputed-identity exchange when available. Score whether the specialist accurately named the firm, identified the official source, explained the claimant's direct filing option, described contractual fees without exaggeration, and avoided claiming government affiliation. Use recordings only where the required consent and recording rules have been satisfied; otherwise audit contemporaneous notes and the script version. A scripted conversation can remain humane and flexible while keeping factual claims stable. Correct a misleading statement promptly, document the correction, and revise the specific sentence that caused the problem before the next similar contact.

Keep claimant identification, addresses, signatures, banking details, and probate records in an encrypted case repository with role-based access and individual accounts. Use encryption in transit and at rest, multifactor authentication, device encryption, expiring document links, and encrypted backups with tested restoration. The abstractor normally needs property records rather than banking instructions; the outreach specialist does not need every probate attachment. Exchange sensitive packets through the protected repository instead of open email attachments or shared personal drives. Log access and downloads, revoke access immediately when assignments end, and document a retention schedule tied to contracts and applicable duties. Do not place identification numbers in task titles, public calendar invitations, or spreadsheets distributed to unrelated vendors.

Section 6801 of Title 15 states the privacy and safeguarding policy for customers of financial institutions and describes objectives for administrative, technical, and physical safeguards. Determine whether the particular recovery business and activities fall within applicable financial-institution definitions and implementing rules; do not claim that every recovery firm automatically has identical obligations under that section. The controls described here remain practical operating choices regardless of that determination. Test one lost-device scenario and one mistaken-recipient scenario before expanding the desk. Identify who disables access, preserves logs, contacts counsel, and evaluates notification requirements. Combine communication findings, access exceptions, filing errors, and aging trends in the weekly operating review so growth reflects reliable execution rather than merely more records in the queue.

chapters.question_prompt: Q12: What should a surplus recovery operator do in the first thirty days?
chapters.title: The First 30 Days: Step-by-Step Surplus Implementation Plan
chapters.subtitle: From county statute selection and O&E title scrubs to your first verified claim packets.
chapters.executive_summary: The first month should produce a documented county strategy, thirty evidence-backed title screens, twelve carefully selected claimant investigations, and a reproducible packet workflow. Begin with official statutes and clerk procedures, then engage state-qualified counsel before contacting prospects. Separate posted balances from recoverable equity and distinguish a negative database search from proven entitlement. Spend the final week executing supported claims or rehearsing packet quality control when signatures are unavailable. Judge the pilot by evidence completeness, acquisition economics, and a funded 180-day runway, not by an assumed first-month payout or a target number of signed agreements.

key_metrics.label: Market
key_metrics.note: Choose documented volume and accessible official records.

key_metrics.label: Underwriting
key_metrics.note: Screening threshold, not evidence of claimant equity.

key_metrics.label: Outreach
key_metrics.note: Contact only supported candidates; do not fill a quota with weak files.

key_metrics.label: Liquidity

sections.heading: Days 1-7: Select the counties and document the rules
paragraphs: Day 1 defines the pilot's cash ceiling, accountable operator, and available weekly hours. Day 2 compares official excess-proceeds inventories and sale calendars to choose two high-volume tax-deed or foreclosure counties in one or two states. Volume means a dated count of plausible balances and recent sales, not a marketing claim about a state. Prefer counties with accessible docket records, recorded instruments, and a clear clerk contact channel. Keep tax-sale and mortgage-foreclosure routes in separate columns because the same county can administer them under different statutes. Record the selection rationale and a backup county, but do not launch a third queue before the first two have usable forms and a documented review process.

Day 3 opens a jurisdiction matrix for each selected sale type. Capture claimant eligibility, priority, claim deadline, fee caps if applicable, contract restrictions, assignment requirements, waiting periods if applicable, and the official authority for each entry. Mark uncertain entries unresolved rather than copying assumptions from a neighboring state. Florida section 197.582 addresses tax-deed surplus distribution; California Revenue and Taxation Code section 4675 addresses claims to excess proceeds from tax-defaulted property sales. Neither citation should be casually substituted for a mortgage-foreclosure rule. Separate the statute's text from counsel's interpretation and the clerk's administrative instructions. Preserve retrieval dates and section references so a later rule change can be traced to the affected files and outreach language.

Day 4 downloads current clerk claim forms, instructions, proof-of-identity requirements, and sample filing receipts where available. Day 5 checks the forms against the matrix and sends specific unresolved questions to a licensed foreclosure or probate attorney qualified for the chosen matters. Day 6 agrees co-origination terms with that attorney, spelling out claimant representation, conflicts, referral arrangements, fee allocation where permitted, costs, custody of documents, and responsibility for filing. Do not assume a nonlawyer may share legal fees; structure compensation around applicable professional rules. Day 7 signs the supported arrangement and freezes the pilot checklist. If a second state requires additional counsel, secure that coverage before its files advance to legal work rather than treating one attorney's license as nationwide authority.

sections.heading: Days 8-14: Underwrite thirty balances, not thirty names
paragraphs: Day 8 retrieves the official county excess-proceeds lists and preserves the original documents, publication dates, and source URLs. Day 9 normalizes parcel identifiers, case numbers, sale dates, apparent owners, and gross balances, then removes duplicates and filters balances below $15,000. A posted balance is only an intake signal: disbursements, superior claims, stale postings, and administrative adjustments may already have changed it. Confirm the current amount through an official record or permitted clerk inquiry before spending heavily. Create thirty numbered pilot files with immutable source references. If fewer than thirty meet the criteria, record the shortfall and continue the supported sample; lowering the threshold merely to fill the worksheet corrupts the pilot's economics.

Days 10 through 12 run grantor and grantee vesting searches and ownership-and-encumbrance, or O&E, scrubs on ten files per day, adjusting the pace if records require more work. Link the sale account to the correct legal description and trace conveyances through the relevant entitlement date. Search former names, trusts, estates, entity variations, and recorded interests against the appropriate county index. Identify mortgages, judgments, tax liens, assignments, releases, probate documents, and potentially competing interests. A deed alone does not establish who receives every dollar. Keep an instrument-by-instrument timeline, with recording number and unresolved effect, and send legal priority questions to counsel rather than deleting a lien because it is old or absent from a commercial summary.

Day 13 reconciles the thirty O&E bundles with the current surplus evidence and creates a provisional waterfall for each file. Subtract only documented allowances and claims in a counsel-supported priority order, keeping uncertain deductions visible as ranges. A $40,000 posted balance with $18,000 of potential superior claims and $2,000 of authorized costs suggests $20,000 of provisional claimant equity, not a $40,000 fee base. Day 14 ranks candidates by supported net equity, record completeness, deadline proximity, and contact feasibility. Select up to twelve lien-clean candidates, meaning the surviving-interest review supports outreach rather than that every search can prove an absolute absence of liens. Preserve rejected files and reasons so the principal can distinguish poor county inventory from weak search execution.

sections.heading: Days 15-21: Verify people and explain the offer accurately
paragraphs: Day 15 skip-traces the top twelve supported claimants using permitted sources and stores provenance for each address and telephone number. Match multiple identifiers without spreading sensitive personal data into the general task queue. Day 16 checks probate authority, trust capacity, entity status, and name collisions before assuming the located person can sign. A surviving family member is not automatically the authorized estate representative, and a former officer may not bind a dissolved entity. Suppress wrong-party contacts and record the reason. If a claimant declines further contact, update all active contact channels rather than relying on one employee's notes. Never discuss the apparent surplus with unrelated neighbors or employers simply because they answered a tracing call.

Day 17 searches PACER for relevant bankruptcy cases using verified names and appropriate identifiers, then has counsel evaluate matches, discharge records, trustee authority, abandoned property, and pending proceedings where material. A negative PACER search is evidence of the search performed, not universal proof of bankruptcy clearance. Record query date, identifiers, result, reviewer, and remaining limitations; use current docket records to resolve matches. Refresh this review before filing if time or new information warrants it. The operational aim is bankruptcy-clear routing supported by counsel, not a checkbox that silently ignores unresolved cases. Hold affected outreach or contracting steps when authority is uncertain, while continuing supported files that do not depend on that unresolved question.

Day 18 prepares transparent verification packets naming the official source, the firm's private role, the claimant's option to approach the clerk directly, the proposed fee basis, anticipated costs, and uncertainties in amount and timing. Day 19 sends packets through approved contact channels and logs delivery without treating delivery as agreement. Day 20 conducts scripted conversations and records them only where applicable recording and consent requirements are satisfied; otherwise use structured contemporaneous notes. Explain that posted surplus can be reduced by competing claims. Day 21 audits the first interactions against the actual documents, corrects misunderstandings, and schedules only supported signings. Measure verified contacts and informed decisions separately from signed contracts so the team does not improve its apparent conversion rate by pressuring confused recipients.

sections.heading: Days 22-30: Execute packets and decide from measured economics
paragraphs: Day 22 confirms willing claimants, signing authority, document versions, and any required witnesses. Day 23 coordinates the mobile notary and accessible appointment logistics without instructing the notary to bypass identification or presence requirements. Day 24 checks signed pages, certificates, dates, exhibits, legal descriptions, and consistency of claimant names. Day 25 sends complete packets to counsel for final legal review and filing where the route requires counsel; obtain the actual submission receipt and note any clerk deficiencies. If no claimant has signed, run the same sequence on a clearly labeled synthetic or redacted training packet and stop before submission. A rehearsal tests workflow but must never appear in the register as a real filed claim or earned fee.

Day 26 reconciles actual filing acknowledgments, missing exhibits, and claimant updates. Day 27 totals pilot acquisition spending, separating list preparation, title searches, tracing, outreach labor, notary costs, and case-specific counsel charges so nothing is counted twice. Calculate cost per screened file, verified contact, signed engagement, and filed claim using actual denominators; when the denominator is zero, label the ratio unavailable. An illustrative $6,000 spent across thirty screens costs $200 per screen; if three engagements result, acquisition cost is $2,000 per engagement before later servicing costs. Those ratios do not establish profitability. Estimate collection probability and expected net fee contribution separately, document assumptions, and do not present a signed contingent agreement as collected revenue.

Day 28 tests the 180-day reserve runway using available unrestricted cash and forecast operating outflows. At $12,000 monthly cash burn, six months requires approximately $72,000 before a separate allowance for committed case costs and adverse timing; subtract those commitments first when computing runway. Use a dated cash schedule when exact 180-day coverage matters. Day 29 compares findings with the initial spending ceiling and identifies the single largest bottleneck, whether inventory quality, title ambiguity, contact accuracy, or execution. Day 30 records Continue, Revise, or Stop with evidence and a named next action. Continue only when supported economics and cash coverage justify the next cohort; revise a fixable bottleneck with a bounded experiment; stop new acquisition when the model cannot fund its own unresolved exposure. Preserve servicing obligations on existing claims under every decision.

callout.title: Day-30 Continue / Revise / Stop
callout.body: Decide on evidence, contribution economics, and funded runway rather than promised first-month collections.
items: Continue: supported pipeline and adequate cash coverage.
Revise: one bounded, measurable correction.
Stop: cease new acquisition while servicing existing obligations.
